newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dlr dips as budget deficit disappoints.
newsitem.headline: Australian dlr dips as budget deficit disappoints.

text.p: The Australian dollar trembled in late trade after the Federal government's Budget produced a higher than expected estimate for the deficit in 1997/98.

The government projected an underlying shortfall of A$3.9 billion for the next financial year, around A$2.0 billion more than analysts had looked for. The headline suplus was also far smaller than recent speculation had favoured. The disappointment was soothed somewhat by a forecast of a A$1.6 billion surplus in 1998/99 which was better than the straight balance expected.
By 7.40 pm (0940 GMT) the dollar had slipped to US$0.7813/18 from US$0.7826/31 just before the details hit screens.
The dollar had edged higher through the day, partly in anticipation of a tight budget which would cut up to A$2.0 billion in government spending.
The actual cuts were a mere A$352 million, which analysts saw as a worrying sign of a slackening in resolve by the government in adressing Australia's long term savings problems.

The economic forecasts underpinning the budget were deemed mixed by analysts. A GDP growth of 3.75 percent penciled in for 1997/98 melded well with median market expectations of 3.9 percent, but the government saw underlying inflation at 2.0 percent when analysts reckoned 2.5 percent was more likely.
